key_insight: FERMAT shows that the best prediction approach depends on the task: representation-based models work better for long-term disease risk, while generation-based models do better for same-day clinical event prediction.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinicians and health systems choose the right AI strategy for different EHR prediction needs, from future disease risk to near-term event forecasting.
method: Trained a 65-million-parameter autoregressive clinical foundation model on longitudinal EHR data from 3.77 million patients.
Compared representation-based predictors versus generated-sequence predictions across risk and event-prediction tasks.
Evaluated chronic kidney disease, fatty liver, diabetes risk, and same-day diagnoses, prescriptions, and procedures.
evidence_signal: In a 10,000-patient test cohort, representation-based prediction improved five-year disease-risk AUROC by 0.098-0.115, while generation-based prediction reached 71.0% Recall@10 for same-day events versus 55.7% for representation-based prediction.
watch_item: Results come from a single-hospital EHR dataset, so performance may not generalize well to other care settings or coding practices.
paper_title: FERMAT: An Autoregressive Clinical Foundation Model for Disease Risk and Clinical Event Prediction
